fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Verse 2 says they "…stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers." They didn't only own up to their own sins, they owned up to their fathers' iniquities too. That takes some humility, and I know how hard that is when it's your own mess to admit.

That's a fair guess, but this verse doesn't mention any offerings. What it says is that they stood up and "…confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers." The whole moment is about owning up.

Nope, nobody's running for office here. Verse 2 has them separating from the foreigners, then standing to confess "…their sins and the iniquities of their fathers." Picking leaders isn't part of this verse.

Marching to the city gates isn't in the verse, friend. The Levites say, "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting…" The call is to bless the LORD. The people have plenty of time on their feet already.

Moses does show up in this prayer, but not at the start. His name comes in verse 14, after creation, Abraham and Egypt. The prayer opens much earlier, with God who "…created the heavens, the highest heavens with all their host…" It's a long prayer, and it starts way back.

David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), doesn't appear anywhere in this prayer. The Levites open in verse 6 with God who "…created the heavens, the highest heavens with all their host…" Their history starts at the very beginning.
That's what the verse says. The signs and wonders came "…for You knew they had acted with arrogance against our fathers." The Levites also say God made a name for Himself that endures to this day.

Anger is right. Verse 17 says, "But You are a forgiving God, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in loving devotion, and You did not forsake them." Read that one slowly, because it's the center of the whole prayer. It comes right after the people stiffened their necks and appointed a leader to return them to their bondage in Egypt.
Mending is a nice idea, but the verse doesn't mention it. It says, "Their clothes did not wear out…" That was during the forty years God sustained them in the wilderness, so that they lacked nothing.
Stars. Verse 23 says God "…multiplied their descendants like the stars of heaven…" Funny thing, I get a star in my sky for every finished cookie box. Theirs came from God multiplying them.

That's not what happened. Verse 24 says, "You subdued before them the Canaanites dwelling in the land." Israel went in and possessed the land, and God delivered the kings and peoples into their hands.

Picked clean isn't what the verse describes. Verse 25 says they took "…houses full of all goods, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance." It also says they ate and were filled, and delighted in God's great goodness.

Yes, and it's a heavy line. Verse 26 says, "They killed Your prophets, who had admonished them to return to You." The prophets had been urging them to come back. I think that one hurts to say out loud.

That's the reason the Levites give. Verse 31 says, "But in Your great compassion, You did not put an end to them; nor did You forsake them, for You are a gracious and compassionate God." The reason is who God is, not anything they did. I'm glad about that.
Kings is right. Verse 37 says, "Its abundant harvest goes to the kings You have set over us because of our sins." The people go on to say, "We are in great distress."
Prophets come up in this prayer, but not in this blank. Verse 37 says the harvest goes "…to the kings You have set over us because of our sins." Kings is the word that fits.

That's it. Verse 38 says, "In view of all this, we make a binding agreement, putting it in writing and sealing it with the names of our leaders, Levites, and priests." After all that history, they put it in writing and sealed it. A prayer was spoken, and now the names go into the agreement.
